display: Koh Samui / Koh Phangan / Koh Tao
tagline: Three world-famous Gulf islands, one airport, and a 1h45 ferry crossing that the northeast monsoon shuts down — the inter-island gap is the whole opportunity.
summary: The Samui–Phangan–Tao trio is one of Southeast Asia's densest leisure island chains: a million-plus air arrivals into Samui feed a constant flow onward to Phangan's Full Moon scene and Koh Tao's dive schools, plus a wall of luxury resorts (Four Seasons, Six Senses). Every onward leg today is a diesel catamaran ferry that is slow, weather-exposed and routinely cancelled in monsoon swell. Marine mobility here is the missing premium tier — foiling flies above the Gulf chop, links the islands and the airport jetties that already exist, and turns a weather-fragile transfer into a smooth, reliable, near-silent hop.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire Samui–Phangan–Tao triangle sits inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Samui↔Phangan (~12 nm), Phangan↔Tao (~24 nm) and the longest leg Samui↔Tao (~42 nm) all fit with margin for multiple daily rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, would extend the network to the mainland (Surat Thani / Chumphon / Donsak) and across the Gulf without relying on island grid power for charging.

competitive_landscape: The water is run today by established high-speed catamaran operators — Lomprayah, Seatran, Songserm, Raja Ferry — on fixed daily schedules between Samui, Phangan, Tao and the mainland piers. The flows are enormous and proven, but the experience is undifferentiated, weather-fragile and entirely diesel: no on-demand, no premium, no foiling option exists. Cancellations and rough crossings in the monsoon are the recurring pain that a foiling tier directly answers.
seasonality: The Gulf of Thailand's northeast monsoon (roughly Oct–Dec, peaking November) brings the heaviest swell and the ferry cancellations that strand travellers and cut into resort stays — the trio's defining seasonal pain. Foiling above the surface chop is exactly the platform that keeps a crossing smooth and on-schedule through marginal sea-states, converting the monsoon window into the strongest reliability case.
regulatory_note: Operates under the Marine Department of Thailand; inter-island services run from established piers (Nathon, Maenam, Lipa Noi on Samui; Thong Sala on Phangan; Mae Haad on Tao). Koh Samui and the surrounding islands carry growing low-carbon / sustainable-tourism ambitions, and a near-silent, low-wake all-electric foiling fleet aligns with reef and shoreline protection around the dive economy.
